extracted.intended_audience: Individuals (affiliated or independent) applying for the NEH Public Scholar Program to write a book for general readers
extracted.subtask_short: NEH Public Scholar book grant application
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for applying to the National Endowment for the Humanities Public Scholar Program, which funds the creation of well-researched humanities books for broad/general audiences. Covers project eligibility, expected outputs, budget/time limits, application materials, and submission/monitoring procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project purpose and intended readership
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Scholar Program supports the creation of well-researched books in the humanities intended to reach a broad readership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some humanities scholarship is necessarily specialized, but the humanities can also engage broad audiences in exploring subjects of general interest. Such scholarship might present a narrative history, tell the stories of important individuals, analyze significant texts, provide a synthesis of ideas, revive interest in a neglected subject, or examine the latest thinking on a topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanities research grounding
rubrics_metrics.description: Books supported by this program must be grounded in humanities research and scholarship, making appropriate use of primary and/or secondary sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must demonstrate appropriate use of primary and/or secondary sources to ground the work in humanities scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible writing style
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects must be written in a readily accessible style, addressing significant humanities themes in a way that will appeal to a large audience of general readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program favors prose and presentation that are accessible to general readers rather than highly technical or discipline‑specific writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience appropriateness (exclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications to write books directed primarily to scholars are not appropriate for this program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the proposed book is aimed mainly at an academic/scholarly audience (rather than a broad general readership), the project is not a good fit for this grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for digital or web supplements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may seek support for the creation of digital or Web-based products intended to supplement the book that they propose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental digital/web products are permissible as part of a proposal, but they are intended to accompany and enhance the book project rather than replace the book output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: individual applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: The program is open to both individuals affiliated with scholarly institutions and to independent scholars, researchers, and writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both institution-affiliated applicants and independent scholars/writers may apply; projects may be at any stage of development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected output
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grant supports the creation of a book as the primary deliverable; other supplementary outputs may be proposed but the book is central.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum award amount
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget proposals should respect the program's maximum monthly award when planning project finances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Period of performance: Six to twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects must be scoped to fit within a 6–12 month performance period beginning on the program's stated start date(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects may be at any stage of development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants need not have a finished manuscript; proposals can range from early-stage projects to those near completion, provided they meet other program criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov registration and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Register for a grants.gov account as this is vital to the grants process; submit your application package on Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you already have registered, make sure it is up to date. You will receive confirmation messages from Grants.gov at multiple stages—verify receipt of all confirmation messages and check spam/junk folders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Download and follow application materials and guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin by reading the full grant guidelines and studying the application. Download Public Scholar Program Guidelines (PDF/DOC), the Grants.gov application package, and program resources including FAQs and sample application narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you understand all expectations and restrictions for projects delivered under this grant and are prepared to write the most effective application. Use sample narratives and recently funded project lists as models.

rubrics_metrics.name: DUNS number requirement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must comply with the stated DUNS number requirement (obtain and include a DUNS number as required by federal grant procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of recommendation / references
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH requests letters of reference from your recommenders approximately seven to ten days after the application deadline. You will be notified by e-mail when each of your letters of reference has been received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After you have received the fifth Grants.gov confirmation message (confirming NEH received your application), you may check the status of the letters in NEH’s secure area using your NEH application number and Grants.gov tracking number. You are responsible for ensuring your letter writers have received solicitations and submitted letters; you may send reminders (including the upload link) from the secure site.

rubrics_metrics.name: File preparation and PDF requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Download Adobe Reader; Tips for making PDFs are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NEH and Grants.gov guidance on preparing PDF files and other application documents to ensure readability and successful upload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission monitoring and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify you have received email messages from Grants.gov and monitor the status of the submission of your letters of recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants.gov will send up to five e-mail messages confirming receipt and processing; after those messages you can use NEH’s secure area to verify letter receipt and take any necessary follow-up actions.
